schema_version: 1
contract: course_database
engine: PostgreSQL
owner: ms-go-course
migrations: db/migrations
schema_groups:
  catalog: [track, course_level, course_group, position, tech, tech_version, tag, i18n]
  catalog_relations: [track_level, level_course_group, course_group_course, position_course, position_tech]
  content: [course, module, section, lesson, lesson_example]
  lesson_completion: [lesson_completion_policy, lesson_revision, generated_course_revision_receipt]
  content_relations: [course_module, module_section, section_lesson, lesson_relation, lesson_example_relation]
  tasks: [task, task_i18n, task_learning_target, task_test, task_test_i18n, task_test_group, task_test_group_i18n, task_test_variant, task_test_variant_i18n, task_filestorage]
  runtime_metadata: [compose_config, compose_config_tech, code_structure_type]
  import_tracking: [course_seed_import]
  course_planning: [generated_course, generated_lesson, generated_course_request]
invariants:
  - migrations and repository queries change together
  - source_key is stable identity for managed imported content
  - ordered relation rows are authoritative for authored hierarchy placement
  - assessment children and translations remain consistent with their task type
  - task.assessment_purpose is NOT NULL and is one of knowledge_check or diagnostic; legacy rows backfill to knowledge_check
  - task_filestorage references FileStorage-owned objects and replacement must preserve rollback behavior
  - task_learning_target stores ordered opaque concept/capability references and never stores mastery or graph edges
  - generated Course metadata never inserts another hierarchy node
  - generated Course fingerprints and request idempotency keys are unique
  - generated Course publication is atomic and complete; active private hierarchy, examples, knowledge checks, target bindings, and provenance commit together
  - practice-material-fingerprint-v1 identifies reusable lazy one-Lesson Courses without introducing a new hierarchy or student-owned state
migration_safety:
  - inspect all historical up and down files before changing an existing table
  - prefer additive and reversible changes with explicit backfill and constraints
  - migrate-fresh applies only forward files to an empty public schema in lexical order, imports no seeds, stops at the first SQL failure, returns safe JSON, and exits nonzero on every error
  - Taskfile migrate-down drops and recreates the complete public schema and is destructive
  - lesson revisions and generated request revision receipts reject UPDATE and DELETE
  - legacy assignment histories are never fabricated; cutover applies to new assignments
